description: Board Members, uzay keşfinin sınırlarını mühendislik, bilim ve yaratıcılıkla genişletmeyi hedefleyen disiplinlerarası bir ekiptir. NASA Space Apps Challenge kapsamında geliştirdiğimiz Space Mission Design Game projesiyle, uzay görevlerinin tasarım ve planlama süreçlerini etkileşimli, eğitici ve eğlenceli bir deneyime dönüştürmeyi amaçlıyoruz.
summary:
Moon Landing is a pixel-art strategy game built in Unity 6 for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 “Space Mission Design Game” challenge, and it runs in the browser.

Each run gives the player a random mission inspired by a real expedition, from Apollo 11’s first samples and Apollo 17’s orange soil to hunting for water ice in permanently shadowed craters near the lunar south pole. The mission brief lists the science tools the player must bring. In the hangar, players build their own rocket from cabins, bodies and thrusters. Each part has a trade off like: mass, storage, fuel and cost, which together decide how long the trip lasts and how much food and water the crew uses.

On the Moon, players explore an map with a compass and a countdown that runs on their remaining supplies. They succeed only if they reach the site with the right tools before supplies run out. Each success earns a smaller payout while missions demand more supplies, so every launch becomes a tighter budgeting decision until the player’s luck and planning run out.
details: Our project turns real missions into gameplay. Each run assigns a mission inspired by previous missions from NASA, with a brief listing required science tools. Players build a rocket from cabins, bodies and thrusters and buy food, water, fuel and tools; cost, mass, storage and fuel determine trip length and supply use. On the Moon, they navigate through the terrain in order to find the sites where the scientific tools can be used all while supplies run out. Payouts shrink and supply demands grow each mission until the player fails. The game makes mission logistics and lunar science history accessible for everybody. It was built in Unity 6.3 with C# and deployed as a WebGL build on itch.io, with team-drawn and open-asset pixel art. We prioritized scientific accuracy, accessibility and short, replayable sessions.
